title: bee-core::datamark (secret + injection neutralization) with an mjs oracle, then the capture group
action: Two units, in this order. (1) SHARED CONTENT-SAFETY MODULE -- note it is TWO distinct code paths, not one, and both are in scope: (a) `datamark` (packages/bee/lib/decisions.mjs:1047-1054) NEUTRALIZES -- strips ``` fences, strips the role-tag regex /<\/?\s*(?:system|assistant|user|developer|tool)\b[^>]*>/gi, strips the control class [\u0000-\u0008\u000B\u000C\u000E-\u001F\u007F], trims, and wraps the result in guillemets; (b) `assertSafeContent` (decisions.mjs:277-292) REJECTS by throwing, testing SECRET_CONTENT_PATTERNS (decisions.mjs:12-17) and INJECTION_PATTERNS (:22-25). Port both into a standalone crates/bee-core/src/datamark.rs. CORRECTED CONSTRAINT -- the earlier claim that regex-lite is sufficient AS-IS was wrong; review caught it. The construct inventory omitted \s, which appears in FIVE ported patterns: SECRET_CONTENT_PATTERNS[5] (decisions.mjs:17) and all four INJECTION_PATTERNS (:22-25), plus datamark's role-tag strip (:1050). regex-lite's \s is ASCII-ONLY; JS \s is NOT (it is WhiteSpace + LineTerminator regardless of the /u flag). Measured against the real module on this machine: JS \s matches U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000-U+200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000 and U+FEFF. So `ignore\u00A0all\u00A0previous\u00A0instructions` is REJECTED by mjs and would be ACCEPTED by a naive port -- a parity red that is simultaneously a content-safety bypass of the injection guard. CRITICALLY, switching to the full `regex` crate does NOT fix it: that crate's \s is Unicode White_Space, which EXCLUDES U+FEFF, so it diverges from JS in the other direction. The fix this cell must implement is to HAND-ENUMERATE the JS \s set as an explicit character class and STAY on regex-lite (crates/bee-core/Cargo.toml:23, zero transitive deps, pure Rust, musl-clean -- D8 posture preserved, no new dependency). Do the same audit for /i, where regex-lite folds ASCII-only while JS /i without /u does simple Unicode case folding. The \b, \w and \d reasoning DOES hold and stands: those are ASCII-only in JS without /u, matching regex-lite exactly. TWO TRAPS FOUND IN VALIDATION, both mandatory: (i) matrix row 3 -- JS String.prototype.trim() strips U+FEFF but Rust str::trim() does not, and datamark ends in .trim() (decisions.mjs:1052), so U+FEFF in leading and trailing position MUST be a corpus case and the Rust trim must be made to match JS, not the other way round; (ii) matrix row 4 -- the rejection message interpolates ${pattern}, i.e. the JS regex LITERAL SOURCE (decisions.mjs:280-283), so the Rust error text must emit that exact JS spelling (e.g. `/\bAKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}\b/`) rather than any Rust-side Display of its own pattern; a semantically equal message with different spelling is a parity red. Prove the whole module with a file-based oracle test following crates/bee-core/tests/fsutil_oracle.rs: a node child executes the REAL packages/bee/lib/decisions.mjs over an adversarial corpus and the results are diffed against the Rust functions. Corpus must include one case per member of the JS \s set above in INTERIOR position (leading/trailing alone is exactly what the old corpus covered and why it would have gone green on this bug), the /i folding cases, a case separating ASCII \b from Unicode \b (e.g. `éAKIAABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP`), nested and unterminated code fences, every role-tag form incl. closing and whitespace-padded variants, each control character individually, U+FEFF leading and trailing, lone surrogates, CRLF, an empty string, a multi-kilobyte payload, and at least one true positive per secret and injection pattern plus a near-miss negative for each. A pattern that cannot be translated exactly is reported in the worker block as a blocker -- never quietly approximated. (2) CAPTURE GROUP: port capture (packages/bee/lib/capture.mjs, 118 LOC + handlers at packages/bee/bee.mjs:4009-4056) -- verbs add, list, flush, count over .bee/capture-queue.jsonl, bare appendJsonl with NO lock (capture.mjs:80,124), stub content validated through the module just ported — and note the REVIEW CORRECTION: capture.mjs:19,26 iterates the pattern ARRAYS to REJECT at write time; it never calls datamark. The audit surface here is the write-time REFUSAL MESSAGE (decisions.mjs:278,285 / capture.mjs:19,26), not neutralization output. VALIDATION-FOUND OBLIGATION (matrix row 7): crates/queen-bench/src/fixture.rs writes NO capture queue -- zero references to `capture-queue` (verified by grep during validation). Extend fixture::generate to seed a non-empty .bee/capture-queue.jsonl with both stub and flush records BEFORE writing the scenarios, or list/count/flush would diff two empty files and report a meaningless clean. Register --cmd-check scenarios: add with adversarial content; add with content that must be REJECTED (secret pattern) and the refusal text byte-diffed; list/count on an empty and on a corrupt-tail queue; flush; and the stub/flush record shapes byte-diffed. THREE MORE REVIEW ITEMS. (i) crates/bee-core/src/capture.rs ALREADY EXISTS (73 lines, read-only projection) -- EXTEND it, never create a second capture module beside it. (ii) LONE SURROGATES cannot round-trip: JS holds `\uD800` but a Rust String cannot represent it and it cannot survive a UTF-8 pipe from the node child. Pin a bytes-level transport (hex or JSON-escaped on both legs) in the oracle, or drop that corpus item with the reason stated in the worker block -- do not leave it as an unachievable requirement. (iii) THIS CELL ALSO OWNS TWO SHARED CONSTANTS that a later cell needs before its own port lands: KIND_ALIASES (packages/bee/lib/feedback.mjs:67) and NORMALIZED_KINDS (:98). packages/bee/bee.mjs:3687 backlogAllowedTypes() = [...Object.keys(KIND_ALIASES), ...NORMALIZED_KINDS].sort() IS the `backlog add --type` refusal text, a byte-parity surface consumed by rpl-6 which runs BEFORE the feedback port. Put both constants in bee-core here so rpl-6 consumes the enumeration authority rather than hardcoding a second list (a D7 violation). Also assert this group's own unknown-verb usage fallback line (packages/bee/bee.mjs:6586-6609).

truths: cargo test -p bee-core --test datamark_oracle passes, diffing both the Rust neutralizer AND the Rust rejector against the real mjs over every corpus case, with case names printed
the U+FEFF leading/trailing cases pass, proving the Rust trim was matched to JS trim rather than left divergent
a rejected value produces an error message byte-identical to mjs, JS regex-literal spelling included
crates/queen-bench/src/fixture.rs seeds a non-empty .bee/capture-queue.jsonl containing both stub and flush records
cargo run --release --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml -p bee-parity -- --cmd-check --group capture reports every capture scenario clean over that non-empty fixture
the appended jsonl line is byte-identical between runtimes, key order included
no lock is taken by the capture path in either runtime
no new regex dependency was added to crates/bee-core/Cargo.toml

every member of the JS \s set (U+0009-U+000D, U+0020, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000-U+200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000, U+FEFF) matches identically in both runtimes in INTERIOR position, proven per-codepoint by the oracle
the injection guard rejects `ignore\u00A0all\u00A0previous\u00A0instructions` in both runtimes — the exact bypass review found
the write-time REFUSAL MESSAGE is byte-identical to mjs for both the secret and the injection path, JS regex-literal spelling included — this, not neutralization output, is the audit surface
KIND_ALIASES and NORMALIZED_KINDS live in bee-core and the sorted allowed-type list they produce is byte-identical to mjs backlogAllowedTypes()
the capture unknown-verb usage fallback line is byte-identical to mjs

node-child oracle over an adversarial corpus incl. U+FEFF and per-pattern true positives and near-miss negatives
capture queue seeded into the generated fixture

key_links: rpl-4 and rpl-8 consume bee-core::datamark rather than reimplementing it
capture.mjs:11 imports these patterns from decisions.mjs to avoid a module cycle -- the Rust side has no cycle, so datamark.rs is standalone
fixture floors and the REFUSED-on-shrunk-fixture contract at crates/queen-bench/src/fixture.rs:60 must not be weakened by the addition
prohibitions: No edits to .bee/bin/ or packages/bee/ (D1 freeze)
No approximated regex translation -- an inexact pattern is a blocker, not a rounding
No new regex dependency; regex-lite 0.1 is already present and sufficient
No lowering of any existing fixture floor to make room for the new store
Tests never touch the live .bee/ store
No bare \s in any ported pattern — neither regex-lite nor the full regex crate matches the JS set
No second capture module beside crates/bee-core/src/capture.rs
No hardcoded copy of the allowed-type list anywhere — the ported constants are the enumeration authority (D7)

verify: cargo test --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml -p bee-core --test datamark_oracle && cargo build --release --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml && cargo run --release --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml -p bee-parity -- --cmd-check --group capture

trace.outcome: Ported the shared content-safety layer (datamark neutralizer + secret/injection rejector) onto regex-lite with a hand-enumerated JS whitespace class, proven against the real frozen mjs by a node-child oracle; extended bee-core::capture with the add/flush writers; landed the capture CLI group behind the rpl-1 seam; seeded the capture queue into the generated fixture and registered 17 --cmd-check capture scenarios, all clean with every negative control firing. Closes a live injection-guard bypass: interior U+00A0 (and every other non-ASCII JS whitespace code point) sailed through a bare-backslash-s port while mjs rejected it.

deviations.what: cmdcheck.rs test `unported_ledger_groups_still_have_zero_scenarios_registered` asserted capture has zero scenarios
deviations.why: registering the capture group makes the rpl-1 pin false; rewritten around a PORTED_GROUPS list plus an assertion that the pin still guards at least one unported group

deviations.what: dispatch.rs test `the_shipped_table_registers_no_ledger_group_yet` asserted the dispatcher registers NO ledger group
deviations.why: already false after rpl-2; it stayed green only because cargo test aborts after the first failing target and bee-parity failed first. Now an exact-set assertion over the ported groups

deviations.what: lone-surrogate corpus item dropped, with the reason stated in the test module header
deviations.why: a Rust String cannot represent an unpaired surrogate and every path into these functions has already validated UTF-8; stated rather than left as an unachievable requirement (cell review item ii)

deviations.what: capture add parity scenarios run --json rather than text mode
deviations.why: add's human text interpolates a fresh crypto.randomUUID() as bare prose and bee-parity::normalize masks by JSON key name only (deliberately no pattern scrubber); under --json the same value is a real key and masks on both legs

deviations.what: the add-refusal scenarios' negative control is the registry dump, not the capture queue
deviations.why: addCaptureStub refuses before reading or writing anything, so no queue perturbation can move their output - a queue-aimed control there would be a control that cannot fire, turning a missed divergence into a false green
